title: Release packaging can ship without TypeScript or lint validation
reasoning: The release packaging scripts all invoke `npm run build`, but `build` is only `vite build`. Vite's production build generally transpiles TypeScript and bundles assets, while the explicit `typecheck`, `lint`, and Jest test scripts are separate and not part of the package path. A package command can therefore produce distributable artifacts even when type errors, lint-enforced release blockers, or frontend test regressions exist.
recommendation: Make the release packaging path depend on a validation script, for example `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test:ci && vite build`, or introduce a dedicated `prepackage`/`release:check` script used by all package variants before `electron-builder`.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included test or package-script assertion covers the command graph for release packaging; the only evidence shows validation scripts exist but are not wired into `build` or `package`.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small package-script contract test that parses `frontend/package.json` and asserts every release packaging script runs the required validation script before `electron-builder`.
minimumFixScope: Update `frontend/package.json` scripts so package/release commands run frontend typecheck, lint, and CI tests before producing distributable artifacts.
